title: Strings, Numbers, and Template Literals
summary: Calculate event quantities with numbers, then place those results inside readable messages with template literals.

sketchBlocks.title: Numbers turn event data into useful results
Template literals mix text with live values

quizDraft.title: Calculate the remaining seats
quizDraft.prompt: An event has capacity 60 and 42 registered attendees. What does `capacity - registered` produce?
quizDraft.hint: Subtract the registered count from the total capacity.

help.hint_1: Capacity is the total; registered is the amount already used.
help.hint_2: The result answers how many seats are still available.

quizDraft.title: Recognize real interpolation
quizDraft.prompt: Which template literals actually insert JavaScript values? Select all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: Look for backticks plus `${...}` around the values or expressions.

help.hint_2: Inside backticks, `${...}` evaluates a JavaScript expression and inserts its result.

quizDraft.title: Complete the interpolation syntax
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the syntax that inserts an expression inside a template literal.
quizDraft.hint: Look for the choice that marks an inserted expression rather than ordinary grouping.

help.concept: marking an expression inside a template literal
help.hint_1: Parentheses and square brackets have other jobs in JavaScript.
help.hint_2: The placeholder uses a special prefix together with curly braces.

quizDraft.template: Inside backticks, write [blank1] to insert a value.

quizDraft.title: Build the announcement in order
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange the steps for turning capacity data into a readable message.
quizDraft.hint: Calculate the data before placing it in the message.

help.hint_1: The template literal needs the values you want to insert.
help.hint_2: After the string is complete, `console.log` makes the result observable.

tokens: Start a template literal with backticks

quizDraft.title: Calculate money left in a budget
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A budget screen knows the starting budget and what has already been spent, but it still needs the amount that remains. Task: Use `budget` and `spent` to calculate `moneyLeft`, then log the result. Expected result: the Console shows the remaining budget.
quizDraft.hint: The amount left comes from subtraction.

help.concept: Arithmetic expressions can combine named number values and produce a new useful value.
help.hint_2: Assign `budget - spent` to `moneyLeft`, then log it.

quizDraft.title: Build a bus arrival message
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A transit notice has separate route and stop values, but riders need one readable message. Task: Create `notice` with a template literal that includes both `routeName` and `stopName`, then log the finished notice. Expected result: the Console shows one message containing both values.
quizDraft.hint: Use backticks so `${...}` can insert both variable values.

help.concept: Template literals combine text with values from variables.
help.hint_2: Assign the template literal to `notice`, then pass `notice` to `console.log`.
